text:
[IDSP.10.1] What every verb implementation must wire
up. Use as a checklist when adding a verb.

| Step | Concrete action |
|---|---|
| Register adapter | Wire `bridge_<verb>` into `ds_rete_adapter_config_t` in `ds_engine_wire_rete_adapters`; `ds_rete_register_adapters` installs it on the Rete engine. |
| Receive args | The bridge receives typed values in the verb's request struct (e.g. `ds_rete_call_request_t`); no per-arg decode. Arity / type are fixed by the `Action` in the rule's `TerminalNode` atom ([RDSC.4a.8]). |
| Look up callback | Read `engine->dispatcher.<verb>_cb` and `<verb>_user`. NULL handling per the verb's policy ([IDSP.2] silent drop vs [IDSP.6-8] essential). |
| Invoke primary effect | Call the typed callback (or run inline if local-only). Save/restore pending slot if the effect re-enters libds (assert/retract). |
| Emit stream event | Once the engine's own part of the verb succeeds, and before any callback, call `ds_recorder_emit_action_<verb>` ([IDSP.1.4]). A verb whose engine part fails does NOT emit; the callback's outcome does not decide it. |
| Surface errors | Essential-verb failures stash via `ds_engine_set_pending` (the bridge's `essential_fail`); `ds_engine_pump` drains and returns them after `ds_rete_run`. |
| Add a public setter | `ds_engine_set_<verb>_callback` (or `_callbacks` for cache). Lives in `dispatcher.c`. Stores into `engine->dispatcher.<verb>_cb / _user`. |
| Update `ds_dispatcher_state_t` | Add the `<verb>_cb` and `<verb>_user` fields in `dispatcher.h`. Init to NULL in `ds_dispatcher_init`. |
| Add a stream-event union member | If it carries a typed payload (e.g., `ds_call_request_t`-shaped event), add to `ds_stream_ev`'s union in `libds.h`. |
| Add a recorder helper | `ds_recorder_emit_action_<verb>` in `recorder.{h,c}`. |
| Write per-verb test | `test_dispatcher_<verb>` covering registration, decode happy-path, NULL-cb policy, error paths, callback-error propagation. |
| Update `test_action_events` | New scenario verifying the verb emits ACTION_<verb> once its engine part succeeds, whatever the callback answers, and not when its engine part fails. |
